requirements.text: clamp(x, lo, hi) returns lo when x < lo, hi when x > hi, and x otherwise (for lo <= hi).
requirements.reason: The claim guarantees that clamp returns x for every input, including when x is below lo or above hi. For example, clamp(7, 2, 5) is required to return 5 but the claim guarantees 7.

claims.summary: For every choice of three 32-bit inputs, the exported function named “clamp” returns the first input unchanged.
claims.statement:
∀ (x lo hi : BitVec 32),
  FVA.Wasm.Exec.Returns Examples.Mislabeled.Lifted.module "clamp"
    [FVA.Wasm.Exec.Val.i32 x, FVA.Wasm.Exec.Val.i32 lo, FVA.Wasm.Exec.Val.i32 hi] [FVA.Wasm.Exec.Val.i32 x]
claims.name: Examples.Mislabeled.clamp
claims.intent: `clamp(x, lo, hi)` on signed 32-bit ints: `x` clamped into the range `[lo, hi]`.
details: Covers every combination of three 32-bit bit-vectors: the value, lower bound, and upper bound.
All are passed as Wasm 32-bit integer values; the claim does not interpret them as signed or unsigned numbers.
The returned 32-bit value must equal the first input bit-for-bit. No arithmetic or wraparound condition is involved.
Returns additionally requires the module to be instantiable and every call from every fresh instance, under every host behavior, to terminate without trapping and return exactly that value.
caveats: Despite the export name “clamp,” the elaborated claim says the result is exactly the first input for every input; it does not assert clamping or any relationship to the lower and upper bounds.
It says nothing about memory effects or behavior of exports other than this call.
